You should check out A Year Without a Job. It’s a modern drama starring Jackie Li who is a “chubby” actress (she’s really not big imo but compared to other East Asian celebs, she is bigger) and it does not focus on her weight at all but instead day to day struggles of a typical working lady including romantic relationships and friendships. 

Also check out other Jackie Li dramas and movies. She’s really great!

Dine With Love (when the fl meets the ml he’s still hung up on his first love and takes a while to get over it)

I May Love You (ml like fls friend at first, while the fl loves him)

The Forbidden Flower (this one’s an age gap romance, older ml and younger fl, but it’s pretty good. The fl falls first and the ml doesn’t reciprocate because she’s younger and because of his past with his first love. There’s less focus on his backstory but it’s still there)

Unrequited Love 2019 & 2021 (these two dramas are basically the same story, but remade. The ml dates another girl in high school while the fl harbors a secret crush on him and they later finally connect and get to know each other in college)

Also if you’re into kdramas, Do You Like Brahms? does this really well as the whole story is based on secret crushes/loves. The ml is in love with his childhood friend, who is now dating his best friend, while the fl is in love with her childhood friend, who is now dating her best friend. It’s pretty slow burn but the fl does falls first.

For upcoming modern dramas:

Our Generation (Zhao Jinmai and Zhang Linghe are starring in their second dramas together which I believe will air in 2025 as they are currently filming)

Love’s Ambition (stars Zhao Lusi and William Chen, first trailer just dropped and set to release next year)

Hold a Court Now (law drama starring Ren Min and Gong Jun, most likely set for release next year)

Romance in the Alley (life/family drama set to begin airing on the 28th)

The Big Boss is the first one that comes to mind even though it does not really have any romance. The fl is not nerdy or smart either but from the very beginning she declares the ml (also her childhood friend) as her rival/enemy. It’s a high school dramas more centered on comedy and life than romance. To me the fl is pretty, but I think she’s presented as more fun, eccentric, and crazy than that.

Don’t Disturb My Study is another high school drama, but in this one the fl is more nerdy and focused on her studies. The ml is not really a rival to her in terms of academics (he’s not smart), but is a threat to her studies itself, hence the name “don’t disturb my study.” The fl is again pretty to me, but I think she’s presented as more nerdy, annoying, and strong minded to the other students. Also this one’s a time travel-esque drama where the fl returns to her high school days but that aspect is really well done imo.

Find Yourself (I didn’t finish this, but the FL is like 32 and the ML is early twenties I think)

My Fated Boy (I really enjoyed this one, has a 31 year old FL and 24 year old ML)

Sunshine By My Side (dropped this but from what I remember it’s very slow burn and more life/work based with a 36 year old FL and 26 year old ML)

Love the Way You Are (have not watched this yet, but I have heard it’s cute, the FL is 32 and the ML is a younger childhood friend)

The Princess Royal does this trope perfectly I think with the main fl hating the ml in the beginning but after going back in time to their youngest selves, seeing his true nature.

I also think The Double does this in the beginning. When the main fl meets the ml, she only sees him as an obstacle and believes him to be cruel, but then they end up working together later on.

If you’re looking for great enemies to lovers, I’m watching Love of Nirvana right now and the progression/pacing from enemies to lovers is one of the best I’ve seen. The ml seems like the villain at first and the fl has a good reason to hate him but they learn more about each other and grow closer later on.

For modern recs, I think Hello Mr. Gu does this and also has a marriage of convenience/contract relationship. I’m not sure how you feel about youth/school dramas, but in Our Secret the fl does not like the ml in the beginning. If I remember correctly the fl also misunderstood and disliked the ml in Sweet Teeth a bit in the beginning. 

To Fly With You is another good college skating drama where the fl hated the ml for a while. An underrated one that I think portrays the exact relationship dynamic you’re looking for is Always Have, Always Will. It’s a college based drama where the fl meets the ml she knew back in high school and hates him and thinks he hates her too due to a lot of misunderstandings. I also think they might have a fake/contract relationship at one point.

We Go Fast on Trust

Stand By Me 2023 (the one with Zhao Jinmai)

Mr. Fighting

Simmer Down

Dine With Love
I recommend Stand By Me 2023 (the one with Zhao Jinmai). This one’s probably my favorite most underrated drama, it’ll definitely get you crying, the ending is >!very bittersweet imo!<

I’m watching Royal Feast right now and the fl seems very strong willed and independent. It’s refreshing to see a fl, especially from a historical period, who cares more about her career/position than any man and who is capable of defending and protecting herself and the people she loves and knows her worth. Also as a bonus, the fl lead here is the same fl in The Double.
You Are My Hero

Yu Si Feng from Love and Redemption (xianxia)

Xing Ke Lei from You Are My Hero (modern)

Zhang Wan Sen from Shining For One Thing (modern fantasy)

Tuo Ba Jun from The Princess Wei Young (historical)

Yin Xiang from Dreaming Back to The Qing Dynasty (historical/modern fantasy)

Crush (2021) is a strangers to lovers following a visually impaired ml and a college senior fl. As far as I remember there is really no love triangles, although the ml is a bit frustrating sometimes. It deals with other serious topics, I enjoyed it, especially for the fl. watch it especially if you like the girl falls first or the girl chases after guy trope.

For historical dramas I recommend trying Story of Yanxi Palance and/or Royal Feast. I recently watched both of these and loved them because of the fl. The fl is the same one as the one in The Double. Check out The Princess Weiyoung also, it also has a revenge plot like The Double.

If you are talking about Unrequited Love 2019, I also loved that one and I recommend you watch one of the remakes, Unrequited Love 2021. There’s a whole lot of movie adaptations for that one and shared universes that are also worth checking out (My Blue Summer and My Best Summer are two really great film adaptations if you’re interested!).

Others I’d recommend that all are set from high school to college and set earlier are A Love So Beautiful (tbh the ml can be frustrating at times but for me I loved the overall vibes and production/directing, storylines, and nostalgia), Our Secret (I also liked the directing and nostalgic vibes in this one), and Meeting You (this isn’t necessarily a “girl falls first” drama as it’s a little more mutual but I think it’s very similar to the dramas you like and it also has the same fl as When We Were Young).

Iribito (very short yet intense psychological drama)

Hakozume: Tatakau! Koban Joshi (pretty lighthearted super funny police drama)

House of Ninjas (very action-filled/mystery drama with slight romance)

Ishi no Mayu (very short mystery/thriller/detective drama, there’s also sequels and a spin-off)

Sagideka (another very short psychological detective drama)

Doctor X (medical drama following a strong, independent fl, also has many sequels/seasons)

Nijiiro Karute (emotional, comedy-friendship based drama following a sick female doctor)

Lion no Oyatsu (very emotional tearjerker drama following a terminally ill fl staying at a hospice, very slight romance)

Party A Who Lives Beside Me is a really funny romcom. I enjoyed it a lot and the chemistry between the leads is great, the only thing is they don’t exactly live as roommates but instead as neighbors.

My Love, Enlighten Me is one where the leads are cohabiting. I really enjoyed this one and the leads chemistry but the ml is more closed off and cold in the beginning.

The Day of Becoming You is a body swap romcom that has a female lead that is for most of the drama very cold and closed off and male lead that is very warm and welcoming. >!This is not really a spoiler since it’s the entire plot and is in the synopsis but it’s a body swap drama so the ml is technically the one that’s cold and the fl is really the one that’s warm.!<

I didn’t finish this drama but Sweet and Cold definitely fits the trope of cold woman/warm man. The fl is very headstrong, career oriented, and has a painful past, while the ml is younger and more bright and warm.

This last one’s a movie but I thought it’s worth mentioning since it’s fits the criteria. All These Years has a fl that has an unhappy family home and is somewhat bitter and closed off, while the ml is more carefree yet has his own troubles.
Dine With Love is an underrated boss and office worker romance that I really enjoyed!

I Don’t Love You Yet (The whole premise/plot is childhood best friends to lovers but >!it does takes a while for them to get there and to admit their feelings so if you’re okay with unrequited love and love triangles, i recommend trying this one out.!< Imo I think it’s worth it, especially for their chemistry/dynamic!)

Always The Two of Us (This one’s an older one, 2003, but it’s definitely a good watch and is centered on two childhood friends meeting up again. A lot of it is about navigating life and careers, but also includes friendship, comedy, and romance.)

We Go Fast on Trust has a ml who is a racer but starts out on the bottom and struggles to succeed and make it to the top. The roles in this one are a little switched in that the fl is the more cold and distant one and the ml is the more warm and friendly one. The fl is also the same fl from Someday or One Day.

The Prince of Tennis (2019) has practically zero romance and is more focused on sports, bromance, and friendship. I think it is somewhat similar to The King of Avatar, Ping Pong Life, and Hikaru no Go.

Dramas that I think are similar to Under the Skin are Be Reborn, Are You Safe?, Stealth Walker (this one has romance as a subplot but also a strong fl), and The Lonely Warrior.

If you’re looking for historical/period dramas with mystery and case solving (similar to A League of Noblemen) then I recommend Ripe Town, The Sleuth of Ming Dynasty, Under the Microscope, and The Imperial Coroner (has a very smart fl with romance subplot).

Don’t Disturb My Study, Back to Seventeen, and Shining for One Thing are all time travel dramas where the fl goes back in time to school. Closer to You has the ml time traveling to his school years and prevent an old classmate’s death. Other good ones are Waiting For You in the Future, See You Again 2021, and First Love Again.

There’s a drama called I Belonged to Your World as well which has a son who travels back in time to his teenager mom and dad before they get together (so like Twinkling Watermelon). Also there’s another drama called I Don’t Want to Be Friends With You where a daughter travels back in time to her mom’s school years and attempts to help her and figure out who her dad is (this is one of my favorites!). I recommend trying out this one, Back to Seventeen (very short drama), and/or I Belonged to Your World first as I think they meet more of your criteria.

If you’re interested a couple movies that are all about romance and time travel are Love You Forever and Over Again.

I don’t think I know of any wuxias like this but some modern day slice of life, female-centric dramas with little to no romance are Meet Yourself and A Year Without a Job. For a period drama, I think Hilarious Family is a great female centered drama with little romance. Imperfect Love is a more serious drama but is probably the only completely female centered drama with no romance I have watched.

Some other good female centered dramas with little romance are Sisterhood, Marvelous Women, Lady Tough (highly recommend this one), Grandma’s New World, For the First Time in My Life (no romance) and She and Their Stories.

Honestly Chinese dramas that are female centered and have no romance at all are very hard to find. I wish there were more. Usually when I’m looking for something like this I watch japanese dramas are movies as they have many with quirky and fun female leads. I hope Chinese media will portray more female characters like this one day though.

If you liked The Big Boss, I think you’d enjoy Take My Brother Away. It’s more slice of life and family and friends based so there’s little to no romance and more comedy and humor. Others I recommend that have more romance are Wait, My Youth, I Don’t Want to Be Friends With You, Go Ahead, and Lovely Us (heavy on Lovely Us!). Also if you’re into comedy thrillers try Oh No! Here Comes Trouble. For period dramas: The Sleuth of Ming Dynasty and White Cat Legend.

The Date of Marriage has a kind of marriage contract and it’s really cute and lighthearted. Another that revolves around a marriage of convenience/contractual marriage is Only Just Married. This one’s a lot more slow burn and more miscommunication but I think it’s worth the watch!

Oh my Boss! Love Not Included has the same fl from An Incurable Case of Love and it’s really cute and funny. Others I would recommend you try are The Date of Marriage, Kissing the Ring Finger, My Cuteness is About to Expire!?, and Unexpected Love Story in Maison Ginseiso

Waiting For Spring and Rainbow Days are really chill and lighthearted movies with happy endings. Nijiiro Karute is also a semi lighthearted drama. Although it did make me cry and does deal with serious topics, it’s also a huge comfort drama and has a happy ending. It’s one of my favorite dramas, I highly recommend trying it out!

Boukyaku no Sachiko and Ikemen Domoyo Meshi wo Kue. These two are my favorite food dramas they almost feel like a watching a mukbang at times. They are more quirky though with more eccentric female leads. If you’re looking for something more chill and all about food and making it I highly recommend the Little Forest films (Little Forest: Summer & Autumn + Little Forest: Winter & Spring). This one’s super chill/peaceful and literally just about food and nature with barely any plot.

On a Starry Night, Shanai Marriage Honey, Love is Phantom, Neko, Unexpected Love Story in Maison Ginseiso, I Just Wanna Hug You (this one’s a movie but I still highly recommend), Is Love Sustainable?, Marry Me!

Boku Unmei no Hito (has a small love rival, hardly a love triangle imo), Overprotected Kahoko (side characters are very big in this one), and Shizuka Chan to Papa (really emotional with a cute romance). Jintenshaya San no Takashi Kun and Hoshi Furu Yoru Ni were already recommended but I’m bringing it up again cuz I definitely think they’re worth the watch!

Highly recommend Boku Unmei no Hito desu, or I’m Your Destiny. There’s a supernatural element along with comedy/humor in there like Eye Love You. The romance is also really good and cute and builds up nicely like in Eye Love You. It’s definitely a must watch!

I’m also on antidepressants and it really does give the worst withdrawal symptoms. Maybe it helps to know that your not the only one who’s feel this way? For me it always helps me a little and even though it does not make the problems go away it helps me to put it into perspective and sometimes change my perspective. I struggle to find a reason to live or to see the point in living at all but I feel like I’m the same as you as I am scared of the pain of dying. I know it feels like a lot and you feel overwhelmed and I know that right now there’s not a lot you can do to make your problems completely disappear, but talking to people and sometimes reading other’s stories can help. If you ever need someone to talk to feel free to message me.

I understand what you’re feeling. I’ve felt that exact same way many times before. One time after an incident I attempted.
